why: Universe 0 for all of A's theorems. A_to_B: (0) is the non-item definition_16_2_3; (1)–(3) come from ScMap.tangent_mk, tangent_id (with ScMap.id_eq) and tangent_mk_comp. B_to_A: tangent_equiv from (1), tangent_id from (2), tangent_mk_comp from (3), and from these tangent_comp, tangent_comp_of_isEffective, theorem_16_2_4 and theorem_16_2_4_eff. blind_exposure: The writer of B had #printed PolyfoldStructure.Lemma_16_2_1, the statement of Lemma 16.2.1 (if two isomorphisms (f, 𝔣), (g, 𝔤) of polyfold structures have f = g, then 𝔣 = 𝔤 and T𝔣 = T𝔤), which the project records as not holding as read. B does not use it: B's well-definedness clause (1) is about classes under Definition 16.1.6 and holds through MapRep.tangent_equiv. This does not affect the verdict.
overlap: HARNESS: ScMap.tangent is a Quotient.map whose proof argument is the banned tangent_equiv (inline, not a _proof_N). EffPolyfold.tangent carries the banned IsEffective.tangent inline in its structure value. EffPolyfold.tangentFunctor's fields use tangent_id and tangent_comp_of_isEffective. The statement of tangent_comp_of_isEffective itself contains the proof term hd.tangent, so A mentions IsEffective.tangent directly. Plain #rt_check and #rt_check_soft therefore fail on every term mentioning A, each reporting the effectiveness block. A local #rt_check_stmt passes on A_to_B, B_to_A, main_A_to_B and main_B_to_A. It is #rt_check without following the values of ScMap.tangent, EffPolyfold.tangent(._proof_1) and EffPolyfold.tangentFunctor, and it treats IsEffective.tangent, which occurs inside the statement A, as an atom; the proofs use the copy IsEffective.tangent' (checked by grep). rt_overlap B_to_A: 1879 shared project theorems. They are mostly the tangent ep-groupoid / M-polyfold machinery under the statements, plus the lemmas of the copied proofs: tangentMap_comp, isGeneralizedIso_tangentHom, tangentMorCLM_apply, isLocalScDiffeo_src, dense_smoothSet, isEffective_iff_trivialSubgroup_eq_bot.
